abstract:
Adipose tissue is with endocrine properties and secretes many cytokines. Some of these cytokines are concerned with ischemic heart disease. I hypothesized that significant surgical reduction in adipose tissue mass leads to decrease in its cell population which may pose significantly reduced production of adipokines ( Leptin and Angiotensin) associated with ischemic heart disease in obese people.

Study objectives are analysis of Leptin, Angiotensin-II, mRNA expression analysis of leptin, leptin receptor and Angiotensin-II. investigation of genetic variations in the Leptin, Leptin receptors, Angiotensin-I and Angiotensin-II receptors, confirm SNPs of selected sample. Ddetermination of the association of genetic variation in Leptin receptor, angiotensin-I and Angiotensin-II receptors with Leptin and Angiotensin-II levels and determination of effect of genetic variation on the transcriptional regulation.

Case control study having 212 patients (106 patients in each group) with type I Obese adults, both males and pre-menopausal females belonging to ASA 1 and 2 requiring stagged liposuction will be included. Exclusion of subjects with Diabetes mellitus, Metabolic syndrome, Endocrine disorders, on statin drugs, not willing to participate.

After informed consent, blood samples will be taken to quantify plasma levels of Leptin and Angiotensin II pre-operatively by ELISA.

DNA will also be extracted from blood and SNPs will be analysed. The selected SNPs will be amplified by PCR and product will be purified and analysed by agarose gel electrophoresis.

Patients will undergo liposuction and RNA will be isolated from subcutaneous adipose tissue for reverse transcription.

After 3 months, patients will be called back for second session of liposuction and plasma level of Leptin and Angiotensin II will be quantified again. Similarly, expression profile of transcription factors will also be analysed again. Paired t-test will be used to compare clinical parameters like serum adipokines levels and adipokines expression levels and p value \<0.05 will be taken as statistically significant. The results will be utilized to determine impact of surgical reduction on plasma level and expression of the adipokines in minimizing cardiovascular risk factors.
description:
INTRODUCTION:

Overweight and obesity belong to the main public healthcare problems in many developed countries. Causes of obesity are considered to be the combination of genetic, epigenetic and environmental factors. In case of morbid obesity, the human organism suffers from an excess of subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue.1 Adipose tissue plays a principal role in overall metabolic homeostasis, and its dysfunction can lead to metabolic disorders, most notably type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.2 Mature adipocytes express all components of the renin- angiotensin system (RAS) including angiotensin Il (Ang II), and also express the type 1 (AT1) and type 2 (AT 2) angiotensin receptor subtypes.3 For cardiovascular disease, perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) is a specific adipose tissue and now recognized to be an endocrine organ with important physiological and pathological effects on vascular homeostasis and vascular diseases.(4) PVAT dysfunction may induce several pathophysiological states such as obesity, atherosclerosis or hypertension.4-6 There are essentially two major types of adipose tissue with different functions: brown adipose tissue (BAT) containing multiple lipid droplets and densely packed mitochondria, and white adipose tissue (WAT) with large lipid droplets and relatively low expression levels of UCP-1(mitochondrial uncoupling protein-1).4 Ang II is produced from angiotensin I (Ang I as a result of the catalytic action of angiotensin-converting enzyme I (ACE-1). Ang Il plays an important role in the regulation of blood volume, blood pressure, cardiac function, and electrolyte balance.7 On the other hand, Leptin is a protein classified within the adipokine family and is currently recognized as a hormone consisting of 167 amino acids with a molecular weight of 16 kD. It is predominantly synthesized in adipocytes, and its production is contingent upon the volume of fat deposits in the body. It is known that leptin inhibits the orexigenic pathway and stimulates the anorexigenic pathway, underscoring its pivotal role in body weight regulation.8 The relationship between leptin and the RAAS is bi-directional. Leptin not only stimulates sympathetic nervous system activation and angiotensin-dependent mechanisms, but it also seems to be a major driver in the aldosterone production in obese patients.9 Moreover, leptin appears to play a role in heart protection. The increased blood volume in obese patients increases cardiac output and stimulates biomechanical stress and structural remodeling that may result in cardiac hypertrophy. A correlation between plasma leptin levels and cardiac hypertrophy has been clinically demonstrated.10 There is evidence for both angiotensin and leptin receptors in several brain regions involved in regulation of sympathetic nerve activity. Ang II may modulate the action of leptin and adiponectin in obesity. Blocking of RAS increases plasma adiponectin suggesting a role of Ang II in decreased levels of adiponectin. Supporting this, Ang I1 infusion decreased plasma adiponectin and adiponectin mRNA in adipose tissue. Ang II also interacts with adiponectin in their target cells.11 Considering the role of Ang II and Leptin in the regulation of obesity, I hypothesized that significant surgical reduction in adipose tissue mass leads to decrease in its cell population which may pose significantly reduced production of adipokines associated with ischemic heart disease in obese people.

OBJECTIVES:

Analysis of adipokine levels (Leptin, Angiotensin-II) in patients with type I obesity (Quazi Experimental).

mRNA expression analysis of leptin, leptin receptor and Angiotensin-II (Quazi Experimental).

Investigation of genetic variations in the Leptin, Leptin receptors, Angiotensin-I and Angiotensin-II receptors (Case Control).

Confirm SNPs of selected sample. Determine the association of genetic variation in Leptin receptor, Angiotensin-I and Angiotensin-II receptors with Leptin and Angiotensin-II levels.

Determine effect of genetic variation on the transcriptional regulation.

OPERATIONAL DEFINITION:

Significant Fat Reduction A removal of 1 liter or more lipoaspirate through liposuction will be considered as significant.

Tumescence Injection of fluid in the fat removal area containing Ringer Lactate each litter with 40ml 2% xylocaine and 1ml of 1:1000 Epinephrine till the area is blanched and showing fountain sign.

Polymorphism Defined a discontinuous genetic variation resulting in the occurrence of several different forms or types of individuals among the members of a single species. A discontinuous genetic variation divides the individuals of a population into two or more sharply distinct forms.

HYPOTHESIS:

Significant surgical reduction of adipose tissue reduces the level of adipokines (Leptin and Angiotensin) associated with cardiac risk in plasma and their expression in adipose tissue.

MATERIAL AND METHODS:

Study design Case control study. Setting The study will be conducted at Advanced Research Centre for Biomedical Sciences (ARCBS), KEMU and Jinnah Burn and Reconstructive Surgery Center / AIMC, Lahore.

Duration The study will be expected to complete within two years after the approval of synopsis.

Sample size Sample size of 212 patients (106 patients in each group) is estimated by using 95% confidence level and 10% absolute precision with expected percentage LEPrs7799039 as in FEN as 19.1% and healthy control as 14.1%.(12) n = Z 1-α/2 \[P1 (1- P1) +P2 (1- P2)\] d2 Z 1-α/2 = confidence level 95 % = 1.96 P1 = population proportion I = 19.1% P2 = population proportion II = 14% d2 = absolute precision 10% SNP analysis will be done in all the 212 subjects with 106 taken as cases (Obese type 1) and 106 as controls (Normal BMI).

Out of 106 cases, liposuction will be performed in selected subjects. Similarly, sequencing will be done in selected subjects. Sampling technique Non Probability Consecutive Sampling.

SAMPLE SELECTION:

Inclusion Criteria: Type I Obese adults, both males and pre-menopausal females, Patients requiring stagged liposuction, American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) class 1 and 2 (as determined by consultant anesthesiologist) Exclusion Criteria: Patients who are with Diabetes mellitus, Metabolic syndrome, Endocrine disorders, on statin drugs, not willing to participate.

DATA COLLECTION PROCEDURE:

Informed consent will be obtained from the study subjects for donation of blood and adipose tissue samples in the proposed study, which will be conducted under a protocol approved by the Institutional Review Board of King Edward Medical University (Appendix I). The information of the study subjects will be kept confidential, and the subjects will be recruited against lab record number or archive number.

Sample Collection: Patients will undergo lipo-aspiration under tumescence by Colman's technique. Each unit of tumescent fluid will include xylocaine 40ml, Hartmann's solution 1000ml and 1ml adrenaline. A multi hole 5mm liposuction cannula attached with suction machine will be inserted through the incisions using controlled back and forth motion. All the patients will be followed fortnightly. Analysis of pre and post procedure blood and adipose tissue samples will be done. For DNA extraction, 5ml blood will be collected.

Quantification of Serum Adipokines levels by ELISA: Serum will be separated after clotting through centrifugation at 3000 rpm and stored at -70°C. ELIS A will be performed on samples by standard protocol for the quantification of adipokines (Leptin, Angiotensin I1) pre-operatively and three months post operatively DNA Extraction: 5ml blood will be collected in EDTA-coated tubes. Genomic DNA will be extracted from whole blood by using commercially available kits.

Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism Analysis of SNPs: The selected SNPs will be amplified by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) by using the primers given in Table 1. Amplicons will be detected on 2.5% agarose gel and stained with DNA gel stain. DNA bands will be detected by gel documentation instrument under UV light. PCR product will be purified by using commercially available kit and digested with restriction enzymes. The restriction product will be analyzed by agarose gel electrophoresis.

Sequencing of SNPs: Sequencing of SNPs will be done using specific primers by Sanger Sequence using ABI 3500, Genetic Analyzer (Applied Biosystems, Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA) and the sequences will be analyzed using the BLAST program at National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI). Amino acid sequences will be predicted by the standard code and will be aligned using the ExPASY online tool for translation. Sequencing will be done on study subjects and compared with same number of healthy persons for comparison.

RNA Isolation and cDNA Synthesis: RNA will be isolated from subcutaneous adipose tissue by using commercially available kits. 1ug RNA will be reverse transcribed using commercially available Transcription First Strand cDNA kit and oligo (dT) primers.

Real-time PCR Analysis for Gene Expression Analysis: Quantitative real-time PCR analysis will be carried out by using SYBR Green real-time PCR Master Mix and an ARIAmix, real-time PCR system (Agilent Technologies). Cycling conditions for real-time PCR will be 3 min at 95°C, followed by 40 cycles of 30 S at 95°C, 30 S at 60°C and 30 S at 72°C. Results will be analysed using the ΔΔCt method and will be presented as fold difference in mRNA level relative to GAPDH. The expression profile of transcription factors will be analyzed.

DATA ANALYSIS PRODECURE:

Data will be entered and analyzed using statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS-26). Quantitative variables like age, BMI, lipid profile and adipokine levels will be presented as mean ± SD. Qualitative variables like family history of obesity, family history of heart diseases and gender will be presented frequency and percentages. Paired t-test will be used to compare clinical parameters like serum adipokines levels and adipokines expression levels. Odds ratio and 95% CI will be used for SNP analysis. Whereas p value \<0.05 will be taken as statistically significant. Pearson equation will be used to determine association of adipokines levels with clinical parameters and expression levels.

OUTCOME \& UTILIZATION:

The results will be utilized to determine impact of surgical reduction on plasma level and expression of the adipokines in minimizing cardiovascular risk factors.

abstract: In vivo genome editing utilizing Cas9/sgRNA ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) holds substantial therapeutic promise, yet rapid bloodstream clearance and degradation of RNPs have hindered its accumulation within the target site and effective gene editing. Herein, we report a supramolecular ternary complex platform where RNPs are co-assembled with tannic acid (TA) and phenylboronic acid (PBA)-conjugated polymers through sequential self-assembly. This ∼30 nm core-shell structure protects RNPs from enzymatic degradation and dissociates selectively at endosomal pH. Upon intravenous administration in subcutaneous tumor-bearing mice, the ternary complex exhibits prolonged blood circulation and preferential tumor accumulation, achieving 37.2% gene editing at tumor sites compared with only 1.5% for free RNPs. The platform successfully disrupts PLK1 in subcutaneous tumors, accompanied by significant tumor growth suppression. This is further applied to a KRASG13D-mutant tumor model, in which treatment delayed tumor growth. By integrating sequential supramolecular self-assembly with stimuli-responsive cargo release, this strategy presents a promising approach for systemic RNP delivery and tumor genome editing.

abstract: In most cells, Malat1 long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons, Malat1 is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. Our study identifies an unexpected functional unit hidden within a widely studied long noncoding RNA.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nemaline myopathy (NM) is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous disease caused by mutations in sarcomere-associated genes, with congenital forms representing the most severe end of the spectrum. Recessive mutations in KLHL41 underlie a severe congenital NM characterized by sarcomeric disorganization and impaired muscle growth. The in vivo mechanisms by which KLHL41 governs sarcomere assembly and growth remain poorly understood.
METHODS: We generated zebrafish models of KLHL41 deficiency by the CRISPR-Cas9 approach to examine the temporal and molecular basis of sarcomere assembly defects in NM. The phenotypic and physiological characterization of skeletal muscle defects was investigated by birefringence, spontaneous coiling, spontaneous swimming behavior, and force generation assays. Structural analyses by electron microscopy and immunofluorescence assessed myofibril organization and sarcomere structures across developmental time points. Quantitative proteomics and biochemical assays were performed to identify perturbations in sarcomeric proteins and associated molecular pathways.
RESULTS: We show that Klhl41b is essential for the formation and organization of sarcomeres, supporting both radial and longitudinal muscle growth. Loss of Klhl41b resulted in reduced sarcomere size, defective sarcomere assembly followed by progressive destabilization of sarcomeres, nemaline body formation, and reduced muscle function. Proteomic analysis in Klhl41b-deficient zebrafish revealed reduced abundance of the sarcomeric troponin complex proteins, altered abundance of components of the translational machinery, and increased abundance of components of atrophy-associated pathways.
CONCLUSIONS: These data show that Klhl41b is required for sarcomere assembly and growth, and its deficiency drives a cascade of structural and molecular changes underlying skeletal muscle hypotrophy and NM pathology. These findings advance our understanding of disease mechanisms and may inform targeted therapeutic strategies to restore sarcomere integrity and muscle function.

title: Klhl41b orchestrates sarcomere assembly and growth to drive skeletal muscle hypertrophy in vivo.

abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a major cause of chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal failure, involving progressive damage to renal cells, including podocytes. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as important mediators of intercellular communication in the kidney by transporting bioactive molecules such as non-coding RNAs. Rab3A, a small GTPase involved in vesicle docking and fusion at the plasma membrane, may influence EV biogenesis and the cargo composition. This study investigated the non-coding RNA content of EVs released by podocytes following RAB3A silencing under diabetic conditions. Cultured podocytes were transfected with RAB3A-specific siRNA and exposed to high glucose concentrations. EVs were isolated from culture media and characterized using complementary techniques, and their non-coding RNA cargo was analyzed via high-throughput sequencing and validated via RT-qPCR. Our results reveal that RAB3A silencing under high-glucose conditions induced significant changes in EV-associated non-coding RNAs, including altered levels of miR-126-3p. The context-dependent regulation of miR-126-3p suggests its involvement in IRS1/PI3K-Akt signaling, potentially affecting the balance between protective and pathogenic responses in the diabetic kidney. Overall, these findings provide new insights into the role of Rab3A in shaping EV cargo during diabetic stress and highlight EV-associated non-coding RNAs as potential contributors to the pathophysiology of DN.

title: Silencing of RAB3A Reshapes the Extracellular Vesicle ncRNA Landscape in Diabetic Podocytes and Uncovers miR-126-3p as a Candidate Mediator of Podocyte Injury.

abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by extensive neural remodeling and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, both of which contribute to disease progression and therapeutic resistance. However, whether nociceptor-derived signals directly reprogram PDAC cells to promote immune evasion remains poorly understood. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized tumor-intrinsic neuroimmune mechanism driven by calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) signaling through the receptor complex RAMP1/CALCRL on PDAC cells. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of Ramp1 or Calcrl did not alter PDAC cell proliferation in vitro but markedly suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival in immunocompetent mice. These antitumor effects were lost in immunodeficient hosts, indicating that the pro-tumorigenic function of CGRP signaling depends on an intact host immune system. Consistently, tumor cell-specific loss of Ramp1 or Calcrl remodeled the tumor immune microenvironment, enhancing CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell effector activity. Mechanistically, CGRP stimulation promoted TGF-β2 expression and secretion by PDAC cells in a RAMP1-dependent manner. Tumor-derived TGF-β2 subsequently acted in a paracrine fashion to suppress CD8+ T-cell activation and cytotoxic function, whereas genetic disruption of RAMP1 or pharmacological inhibition of TGF-β signaling relieved this immunosuppression. Together, these findings define a CGRP-RAMP1/CALCRL-TGF-β2 signaling axis through which nociceptive input is converted into tumor-driven adaptive immune evasion in PDAC. This pathway reveals a previously underappreciated mechanism linking neural signaling to PDAC progression and identifies CGRP receptor signaling as a potential therapeutic vulnerability for restoring antitumor immunity and improving the responsiveness of PDAC to immunotherapy.

title: CGRP-RAMP1/CALCRL Signaling Drives TGF-β2-Mediated Immune Evasion and Pancreatic Cancer Progression.

abstract: Background/Objectives: Papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) is the most common endocrine malignancy and is generally associated with favorable clinical outcomes. However, a subset of tumors develops aggressive phenotypes characterized by increased proliferation, migration, therapeutic resistance, and disease progression. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as important regulators of tumor biology, yet the role of Long Intergenic Non-Protein Coding RNA 1614 (LINC01614) in PTC remains poorly understood. This study investigated the functional role of LINC01614 in PTC and its potential involvement in ferroptosis-associated molecular pathways. Methods: RNA sequencing data from a repository of 44 paired PTC and adjacent normal thyroid tissue samples were analyzed to identify differentially expressed lncRNAs. LINC01614 expression was evaluated in thyroid cell lines, and CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) was used to generate stable LINC01614 knockdown K1 cell lines. Cellular proliferation, migration, clonogenicity, intracellular iron accumulation, lipid peroxidation, cytokine secretion, and ferroptosis-associated gene expression were assessed using qRT-PCR, RNA sequencing, Western blotting, cytokine array analysis, iron quantification assays, and BODIPY C11 lipid peroxidation imaging. Results: LINC01614 was significantly overexpressed in PTC tissues and thyroid cancer cell lines. CRISPRi-mediated repression of LINC01614 reduced cellular proliferation, migration, and clonogenic capacity. Mechanistically, LINC01614 knockdown resulted in an 8.8-fold increase in miR-4521 expression and a 23-fold decrease in IGF2 expression, supporting a potential competing endogenous RNA mechanism. Reduced LINC01614 expression was associated with decreased AKT, GPX4, SLC7A11, and SLC3A2 expression, increased IL-6 secretion, a 3.4-fold increase in intracellular ferrous iron accumulation, and a marked increase in lipid peroxidation following erastin treatment, indicating enhanced sensitivity to ferroptosis. Conclusions: These findings identify LINC01614 as a novel regulator of aggressive PTC phenotypes and ferroptosis resistance. The data support a model in which LINC01614 contributes to thyroid cancer progression through modulation of a miR-4521/IGF2/PI3K/AKT signaling axis and downstream anti-ferroptotic pathways. LINC01614 may represent a promising biomarker and potential therapeutic target in papillary thyroid cancer.

title: Long Non-Coding RNA LINC01614 Promotes Aggressive Phenotypes and Ferroptosis Resistance in Papillary Thyroid Cancer Through a Putative miR-4521/IGF2/PI3K-AKT Signaling Axis.

abstract: There is growing interest in natural bioactive compounds as potentially safer and more sustainable sources of therapeutic agents. Terpenoids, one of the most structurally diverse and biologically active classes of natural products, are derived from repeating isoprene units and possess a broad range of pharmacological and industrial applications. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in terpenoid biosynthesis, structural classification, and therapeutic applications. It also discusses emerging approaches for enhancing large-scale production, improving functional efficacy, and overcoming pharmacokinetic limitations. Attention is given to terpenoids currently undergoing clinical evaluation, along with their progress toward commercial development. Despite substantial preclinical evidence supporting their therapeutic potential, the clinical translation of many terpenoids remains limited. Key challenges include poor aqueous solubility, low permeability, slow dissolution, and high lipophilicity, which can collectively restrict systemic bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy. Moreover, only a relatively small proportion of biologically active terpenoids have progressed to advanced stages of clinical development, highlighting a considerable gap between experimental findings and clinical application. This review integrates current knowledge of terpenoid biosynthesis, biological activities, production strategies, and translational development while highlighting sustainable and scientifically driven approaches that may facilitate their future therapeutic and commercial utilization.

title: Terpenoids: A Comprehensive Review on Biosynthesis, Applications and Enhancement Strategies for Translational Research.

abstract: Background/Objectives: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) remains a major threat to the global swine industry, while the emergence of variant pseudorabies virus (PRV) strains has further complicated disease control in China. This study aimed to develop a PRV-based viral vector platform for PRRSV antigen delivery and evaluate its safety, immunogenicity, and protective efficacy. Methods: A five-gene-deleted variant PRV strain, PRV-JM-DF, was used as the vector backbone. Candidate genomic insertion sites and endogenous late promoters were systematically screened, followed by construction of recombinant PRVs expressing PRRSV GP2, GP3, GP4, GP5, and M individually or as tandem antigen constructs. Recombinant viruses were characterized for antigen expression, replication, and genetic stability. Safety and immunogenicity were initially evaluated in female BALB/c mice, and the leading candidates were further assessed for safety, immunogenicity, and protective efficacy in 18 Landrace pigs of either sex following challenge with highly pathogenic PRRSV HuN4. Results: The TK locus supported efficient foreign-gene expression, and pUL39 exhibited the highest activity among the tested endogenous late promoters. The recombinant viruses retained replication competence and genetic stability. Among the candidates, rPRV-C-4T induced robust PRRSV- and PRV-specific neutralizing antibody responses and showed no obvious adverse effects during the experimental observation period in pigs. Following HP-PRRSV HuN4 challenge, all rPRV-C-4T-immunized pigs survived and exhibited reduced viremia, viral shedding and tissue viral loads, together with markedly alleviated pathological lesions. Conclusions: rPRV-C-4T provided protection against homologous HP-PRRSV HuN4 challenge while maintaining PRV-directed immune responses, supporting its potential as a PRV-vectored multivalent vaccine candidate.

abstract: Human norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide across all age groups, yet no licensed vaccine is available. The major capsid protein, VP1, self-assembles into highly immunogenic virus-like particles (VLPs) that have shown promise in clinical studies. Recently, mRNA has emerged as a compelling platform for norovirus vaccination. However, whether VP1-encoding mRNA can drive authentic VLP formation in human cells relevant to the vaccination environment has remained unknown. In this study, we used multiple human cell lines, including THP-1-derived macrophage-like cells, to model the post-vaccination environment. Transfection with norovirus GII.4 VP1 mRNA or lipid nanoparticle-formulated VP1 mRNA induced both intracellular and extracellular VP1 expression. Sucrose gradient purification and electron microscopy confirmed VLP assembly. These particles retained key antigenic and functional properties, including recognition by norovirus-specific antibodies in human serum and binding to histo-blood group antigens. Collectively, our findings provide direct evidence that VP1-encoding mRNA can generate structurally and functionally relevant norovirus VLPs in physiologically relevant human cell systems. These results strengthen the mechanistic rationale for mRNA-based norovirus vaccines and support their continued development.

abstract:
BMD006 is an off-the-shelf antitumor mRNA vaccine targeting lung cancer and lung metastatic solid tumors.

This trial also further explores the clinical efficacy of BMD006 in combination with Immuno-Oncology (IO) therapy.

abstract: We report the preclinical and early clinical evaluation of in vivo genome editing for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), delivered via a single AAV9 vector. In humanized DMD mice, systemic administration achieved targeted genome editing, partial dystrophin restoration, and improved muscle function. In non-human primates, efficient on-target editing was achieved with no dose-limiting toxicity identified under the conditions tested. In an open-label, dose-escalation, first-in-human clinical trial (NCT06594094), post-treatment muscle biopsies provided early molecular evidence of hfCas12Max-mediated genome editing and detectable dystrophin expression in participants with DMD. However, at the higher dose level (1.0 × 1014 vg/kg), one participant experienced a treatment-related fatal serious adverse event, characterized by marked complement activation and systemic cytokine response shortly after dosing. This work provides initial human proof-of-concept for muscle genome editing while crucially highlighting the critical role of immunologic risks and the narrow therapeutic window of systemic adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR therapies, underscoring the need to develop safer dosing and immunomodulation strategies.

abstract: Plasmodium vivax is a major malaria parasite that causes acute illness in millions of people each year. Transmission-blocking vaccines (TBVs) could contribute substantially to malaria elimination, although none has yet been approved. We previously demonstrated that a nucleoside-modified mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine targeting Pvs25, a leading P. vivax TBV antigen, elicited potent and durable transmission-blocking immunity in mice. Emerging evidence suggests that circular RNA (circRNA) may enhance RNA stability, prolong antigen expression, and potentially reduce manufacturing costs compared with conventional linear mRNA. We therefore developed and evaluated two circular Pvs25 RNA-LNP vaccines: one encoding wild-type Pvs25 and another encoding Pvs25 fused to the MHC class I trafficking domain (MITD). Their immunogenicity and functional activity were compared with those of a linear nucleoside-modified Pvs25 mRNA-LNP vaccine. In mice, a single immunization with either the circular RNA or linear mRNA Pvs25 vaccine induced detectable Pvs25-specific antibodies, while booster immunization substantially increased antibody titers and resulted in complete inhibition of P. vivax development in mosquitoes. Both vaccines also elicited robust Pvs25-specific antibody-secreting cell response and cytokine-producing cellular responses. Together, these findings demonstrate the potential of circRNA as a platform for malaria vaccine development and support further evaluation in non-human primates.

abstract: Advanced therapeutics, including programmable nucleic acid-based therapies (NATs), such as small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), CRISPR-Cas 9 editing systems, modified in vitro transcribed messenger RNAs (mRNAs) and Adeno-associated viruses (AAVs), have the potential to transform healthcare. However, while there have been considerable successes, there have also been notable clinical failures in early-stage human trials, which slowed down the progression of these therapeutic platforms. Multiple trials of NATs have been halted or discontinued, or approved products carry black box warnings as unforeseen or underestimated toxicities and poor efficacy have been observed in humans. There are a variety of reasons for failure of NATs, one of which is that many preclinical studies lack disease modelling in a human-relevant manner and, therefore, do not capture disease-specific effects on therapy tolerability and efficacy. This Perspective provides a short overview of why better human disease modelling is required to understand the potential therapeutic liabilities of NATs across modalities.

abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Apolipoprotein C-III (apoC-III) has emerged as a validated target for lowering triglycerides, triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, and remnant cholesterol. This review summarizes the biology of apoC-III, the genetic and clinical trial evidence supporting its inhibition, and remaining questions.
RECENT FINDINGS: Loss-of-function variants in APOC3 are associated with lower levels of triglycerides and reduced cardiovascular risk. Pharmacologic inhibition of apoC-III with RNA-based agents has led to substantial reductions in apoC-III and triglycerides across familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS), severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG), and moderate hypertriglyceridemia (mHTG). In FCS, agents volanesorsen, olezarsen, and plozasiran have demonstrated reductions in triglycerides and acute pancreatitis. In sHTG, olezarsen has extended this benefit to a larger, multifactorial population. In mHTG, olezarsen and plozasiran lower triglycerides, remnant cholesterol, non-HDL-cholesterol, and apolipoprotein B, but an imaging study with olezarsen demonstrated neutral findings on coronary plaque composition, and cardiovascular event reduction has not been demonstrated. ApoC-III inhibition provides a potent strategy for lowering triglycerides and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins. Its most immediate clinical role is in FCS and sHTG, where prevention of acute pancreatitis is the main objective. Its future as a cardiovascular therapy will depend on whether reductions in remnant cholesterol and apolipoprotein B translate into fewer atherosclerotic events in a dedicated cardiovascular outcomes trial.

abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) poses a significant threat to global public health, and effective preventive measures are urgently needed. The widespread antibiotic resistance of KP underscores the critical need for vaccine-based strategies. Although numerous vaccine candidates against KP have been investigated, none has yet been licensed. mRNA-LNP vaccines against KP have only recently begun to be explored, and their ability to deliver conserved outer membrane protein antigens remains largely untested. In this study, we constructed an mRNA vaccine encoding the highly conserved outer membrane protein X (OmpX) of KP-the first mRNA-LNP vaccine targeting this antigen-and evaluated its immunogenicity and protective efficacy in mice. Immunoinformatics analyses predicted concordance between the in silico and in vivo outcomes: bioinformatics tools were used to evaluate the antigenicity, immunogenicity, physicochemical parameters, and secondary and tertiary structures of OmpX, and the C-ImmSim server was used to simulate the vaccine-elicited immune responses. We then performed mouse immunization and challenge experiments to characterize the humoral and cellular immune responses induced by the OmpX vaccine. The mRNA vaccine was immunogenic in mice, eliciting high titers of OmpX-specific antibodies. OmpX-Fc mRNA-LNPs also induced robust cell-mediated immunity, with significantly elevated IFN-{gamma} and IL-4 levels indicative of combined Th1/Th2 cellular responses. Serum from OmpX-immunized mice promoted significantly greater complement-mediated KP cell lysis than serum from the alum or luciferase mRNA-LNP control groups. Notably, OmpX-Fc mRNA-LNP immunization conferred complete protection against lethal KP challenge, with 100% survival and a significant reduction in visceral bacterial burden. These data establish a promising mRNA vaccine strategy for inducing broad immune responses and promoting serotype-independent immunity against KP.

abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common, often disabling disorder of gut-brain interaction whose molecular basis remains incompletely defined, leaving diagnosis largely symptom-based and treatment largely non-mechanistic. We argue that the serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; hereafter 5-HT, the primary term used throughout, with "serotonin" retained in less technical contexts) signalling axis-positioned at the interface of the gut microbiota, enterochromaffin (EC) cells, enteric neurons, and the mucosal immune system-is a central, unifying integrator of IBS pathophysiology, and that reframing IBS around this axis offers a route toward mechanism-based subtyping and therapy. We first synthesise how microbiota-driven tryptophan metabolism, short-chain fatty acid and secondary bile acid signalling, and epigenetic regulation of tryptophan hydroxylase 1 (TPH1) shape EC-cell serotonin output, before examining the neuroimmune consequences of dysregulated serotonin secretion-mast cell activation, macrophage polarisation, neurogenic inflammation-and the microbiota-serotonin-gut-brain connectome linking vagal afferent signalling, blood-brain barrier permeability, and central neurotransmitter networks. We then discuss molecular stratification of IBS subtypes through serotonergic endotyping-incorporating SLC6A4 and TPH1 polymorphisms, single-cell transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics-and critically evaluate next-generation therapeutic strategies, including engineered probiotic chassis, CRISPR-mediated microbial editing, and AI-guided nanomedicine, distinguishing proof-of-concept findings from clinically validated approaches. We conclude that reconceptualising IBS as a disorder of disrupted microbial serotonergic ecosystems, rather than a purely symptom-defined syndrome, offers a coherent and testable framework for biomarker discovery and precision, mechanism-directed therapy, while highlighting the causal-directionality and clinical-translation gaps that must be closed before this framework can be applied at the bedside.

abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PO) is not merely a consequence of increased osteoclast activity. Estrogen deficiency induces oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization in bone tissue, thereby sustaining osteoclastogenic stimuli and pathological bone resorption. Interferon regulatory factor 5 (IRF5) is a key regulator of M1 polarization, and silencing its gene by small interfering RNA (siIRF5) may attenuate the pathogenesis of PO. However, selective delivery of siIRF5 to M1 macrophages within the osteoporotic bone microenvironment is challenging. Herein, we develop a nanomedicine, termed siP@WM, for programmed sequential targeting of bone tissue and macrophages. The siP@WM integrates a platinum nanozyme core with mesoporous silica shell loading siIRF5. The shell with enlarged pores (10-15 nm) provides effective siRNA encapsulation and programmable surface grafting of two kinds of poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) derivatives. The longer poly(aspartic acid)-terminated PEG chain promotes bone enrichment. ROS-triggered thioketal cleavage shortens this chain, reduces bone-matrix adhesion, and exposes the shorter folic acid-functionalized PEG chain to enhance M1 macrophage uptake. In vitro, siP@WM scavenges ROS, facilitates endosomal escape, achieves approximately 60% IRF5 knockdown, and promotes M2 polarization. In ovariectomized mice, systemic administration of siP@WM ameliorates bone loss, restores trabecular microarchitecture and mechanical strength, and shows no overt short-term toxicity in major organs. Transcriptomic and histological analyses support attenuated AP-1-associated inflammatory signaling, suppressed osteoclast differentiation, and modulated extracellular matrix remodeling. Together, programmed siIRF5 delivery to macrophages in bone tissue combined with ROS scavenging restores bone homeostasis and provides an adaptive biomaterial strategy for PO treatment.

abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have risen to the forefront of modern therapeutics by enabling the clinical success of COVID-19 mRNA vaccines. In order for them to function as drug delivery vesicles, LNPs must have scalable, tunable, and targeted nanoscale platforms whose strengths in versatility, performance, and clinical relevance are driven by key design parameters and formulation strategies. This Tutorial Review traces the historical evolution of LNPs and examines the fundamental design principles governing their structure, physicochemical properties, and biological behavior. It further highlights modern analytical characterization techniques that have advanced mechanistic understanding of LNP composition, morphology, and function as well as targeting strategies to improve LNP delivery to extrahepatic sites. Current translational challenges and emerging advances are also discussed. This Tutorial Review provides a framework for understanding the foundations, current landscape, and future directions of LNP research.

title: Lipid Nanoparticles at the Crossroads of Chemistry and Medicine: A Tutorial.

abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) progression involves cartilage matrix loss and persistent inflammation. This study developed a machine learning-guided and chondrocyte membrane-camouflaged lipid nanoparticle carrying messenger RNA (CM-LNP@mRNA) platform for intra-articular SOX9 delivery. Random forest analysis identified the nitrogen-to-phosphorus and SM-102 ratios as primary determinants with feature importance values of 0.57 and 0.32 respectively. Following ML-guided formulation selection and experimental membrane-coating optimization, the final CM-LNP@mRNA formulation showed an encapsulation efficiency of 95.50% and a particle size of 133.70 nm. Compared with the conventional reference formulation prepared under the same final coating condition, encapsulation efficiency increased from 89.20% to 95.50% and particle size decreased from 145.40 nm to 133.70 nm. Membrane coating shifted the zeta potential from -25.57 mV to -35.07 mV. This transition provided biophysical evidence of successful surface modification. In interleukin-1β-stimulated chondrocytes, CM-LNP@mRNA increased the relative expression of Col2a1 and Acan from 0.20 to 0.33 and from 0.50 to 0.73, respectively, while reducing the relative expression of Mmp3 and Adamts5 from 10.50 to 7.80 and from 4.00 to 2.50, respectively. These alterations indicated a shift toward a matrix-preserving transcriptional state. Downstream matrix metalloproteinase 3 and prostaglandin E2 concentrations decreased from 37.10 ng/mL to 18.50 ng/mL and from 113.70 pg/mL to 76.50 pg/mL by day 7. This reduction demonstrated effective suppression of catabolic and inflammatory activity. In OA rats, CM-LNP@mRNA reduced the osteophyte volume from 4.00 mm3 to 2.00 mm3 and prolonged the thermal response latency from 7.50 s to 11.80 s. These improvements linked cellular metabolic regulation to functional joint recovery. These findings establish a strategy integrating formulation optimization with biomimetic membrane coating to modulate the OA microenvironment.

abstract: MYC is among the most frequently amplified oncogenes in human cancer, yet its intrinsically disordered nature has rendered it refractory to direct pharmacological targeting. Here, we demonstrate that the long noncoding RNA NEAT1_1 functions as a molecular gatekeeper that controls MYC protein stability by regulating its access to the E3 ubiquitin ligase UBR5. We show that NEAT1_1 forms a ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex with both MYC and UBR5, and that NEAT1_1 suppression disrupts this interaction, leading to decreased MYC polyubiquitination and enhanced protein stability. To systematically map the regulatory architecture of NEAT1_1 without altering its abundance, we screened 88 antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) mixmers tiling across the transcript. Strikingly, this phenotypic screen identified region-specific mixmers that elicit bidirectional control over MYC, either driving robust MYC destabilization or promoting its stabilization in a strictly expression-independent manner. Mechanistically, MYC-destabilizing mixmers selectively enhance the interaction between MYC and UBR5 to accelerate proteasomal degradation. A focused CRISPR screen targeting the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway independently validated UBR5 as the essential E3 ligase mediating this mixmer-induced turnover. In vivo, our lead mixmer ASO_#24 significantly suppressed tumor growth in MYC-high xenografts, whereas MYC-low tumors remained unaffected. Our findings reveal that the functional output of a scaffold lncRNA is encoded in its sub-domain architecture rather than bulk transcript levels, establishing domain-specific RNA targeting as a tractable strategy to rewire protein turnover pathways for otherwise undruggable oncogenes.

abstract:
AIMS: Selenoprotein T (SELENOT) is an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident thioredoxin-like oxidoreductase implicated in redox and calcium (Ca2+) homeostasis and protein quality control. Although SELENOT is highly expressed in the brain, its role in hypothalamic pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons, which regulate energy balance, remains poorly understood. We investigated whether SELENOT is required for maintaining ER homeostasis and neuronal integrity in POMC neurons.
RESULTS: Using CRISPR-edited and siRNA-silenced POMC neuronal models together with a POMC-specific SELENOT knockout mouse, we demonstrated that SELENOT loss induces a senescent-like phenotype including cellular hypertrophy, loss of neurite outgrowth, senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, increased P16 and P21 expression, and acquisition of senescence-associated secretory phenotype. Senescence markers were elevated not only in SELENOT-deficient POMC neurons but also throughout the surrounding arcuate nucleus in vivo, suggesting propagation of a pro-inflammatory microenvironment. Mechanistically, prolonged SELENOT deficiency produced selective activation of the ATF6α arm of the unfolded protein response, depletion of ER Ca2+ stores, and profound alterations in N-glycan maturation. Notably, leptin-induced POMC processing and secretion were spared. Glycomics revealed a shift toward immature glycans, whereas thiol-trapping proteomics identified candidate SELENOT interactors linked to ER Ca2+ regulation.
INNOVATION AND CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first evidence that SELENOT deficiency is sufficient to trigger cellular senescence in POMC neurons, acting as a central regulator integrating ER proteostasis, Ca2+ homeostasis, redox adaptation, and glycosylation. These results reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism potentially linking neuronal senescence to hypothalamic dysfunction and suggest that SELENOT-dependent pathways may represent therapeutic targets for obesity, metabolic disease, and age-related neuroendocrine disorders. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 00, 000-000.

abstract: Seasonal influenza and the ongoing emergence of zoonotic influenza viruses, including highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1), remain substantial global public health threats, underscoring the need for rapidly adaptable vaccine platforms. This state-of-the-art review critically evaluates the clinical development of RNA-based influenza vaccines through a comprehensive assessment of ClinicalTrials.gov records and peer-reviewed literature. Candidates were examined across four domains: seasonal influenza vaccines, pre-pandemic influenza vaccines, combination respiratory vaccines, and self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) platforms. Clinical evidence indicates that mRNA influenza vaccines consistently elicit robust humoral immune responses and, in late-stage trials, have demonstrated improved relative efficacy against influenza A compared with conventional influenza vaccines. Reactogenicity is generally more frequent with mRNA vaccines, particularly with respect to transient mild-to-moderate systemic adverse events. However, serious adverse events remain uncommon and broadly comparable to those observed with licensed comparator vaccines. Pre-pandemic and multicomponent mRNA vaccine candidates similarly demonstrate strong immunogenicity, supporting the potential of RNA platforms for both seasonal vaccination and pandemic preparedness. Clinical development of saRNA influenza vaccines has progressed through early-phase trials, although publicly available clinical data remain limited. Regulatory milestones in 2026, including U.S. approval of mRNA-1010 (mFlusiva), the first approved mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine, and European Union authorization of mRNA-1083 (mCOMBRIAX), an mRNA-based influenza-COVID-19 combination vaccine, represent important steps in the clinical transition and implementation of RNA-based influenza vaccination.

abstract: Gene editing enables precise genetic modifications, revolutionizing disease treatment, crop improvement, and biotechnological innovation. VeCas9, a recently identified CRISPR endonuclease from the Veillonella genus, exhibits a broader protospacer adjacent motif recognition range in comparison with the widely used SpCas9 nuclease. However, its working mechanism and potential applications in gene editing still need to be fully characterized. In this work, by integrating VeCas9 into a graphene-molecule-graphene single-molecule junction platform, we carried out label-free, in situ mechanistic studies of VeCas9 function at the single-molecule level with high temporal resolution. Using this setup, we monitored the dynamic interactions between VeCas9, single-guide RNA, and double-stranded DNA in real time, in both stable and transient binding modes. Through temperature-dependent measurements, we determined the kinetic parameters of key steps in the interaction process. Moreover, a series of double-stranded DNA substrates was employed to examine how various sequence mismatches affect the VeCas9 activity, revealing that its sensitivity depends on the position of the mismatch. More importantly, we directly observed VeCas9-mediated R-loop formation and quantified the time scale of single-base expansion events. These single-molecule observations provide mechanistic insights into the Cas9 function and demonstrate the strong potential of high temporal-resolution single-molecule techniques for studying dynamic biological processes.

title: Probing the Conformational Dynamics of VeCas9 Using High-Resolution Single-Molecule Junctions.

abstract: Probe-based PCR assays are commonly used to evaluate gene expression in antisense oligonucleotide (ASO)-treated samples, but assay design and postextraction processing may introduce substantial measurement bias. We investigated workflow-dependent differences in measured knockdown across PCR-based and RNA-sequencing assays using an allele-specific gapmer ASO, targeting a linked single nucleotide polymorphism of a dominant-negative SPTAN1 variant. Exogenous ribonuclease H (RNase H) activity during reverse transcription or ribosomal RNA (rRNA)-depletion inflated apparent knockdown and reduced RNA-sequencing coverage at the ASO-binding site. In droplet digital PCR (ddPCR), allele-specific detection probes overlapping the ASO-binding site produced substantially greater apparent knockdown than nonoverlapping probes, particularly following workflows with active RNase H. Spike-in experiments showed that this bias was not reproduced by adding ASO to purified RNA before complementary DNA (cDNA) synthesis or to cDNA before ddPCR, but emerged when ASO was present during rRNA depletion. Together, these findings show that exogenous RNase H activity during RNA processing and ASO-probe overlap can distort measurements of gapmer-mediated transcript reduction. Poly(A)-based RNA sequencing, reverse transcriptase with reduced RNase H activity, and nonoverlapping PCR detection probes can minimize measurement bias when evaluating gapmer ASO-mediated knockdown.

title: Considerations of Gene Expression Analysis Methods for Gapmer Antisense Oligonucleotide-Treated Samples.

abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Emerging evidence has established N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation as a key epitranscriptomic mechanism underlying hepatocarcinogenesis. Methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3), the catalytic core of the m6A methyltransferase complex (MTC), forms a heterodimer with METTL14 and cooperates with auxiliary components of the MTC to deposit m6A modifications that modulate mRNA stability, splicing, nuclear export, and translation. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the current understanding of METTL3 biology in HCC, focusing on its structure, assembly within the MTC, regulation of coding and non-coding RNAs, and its roles in driving key oncogenic signaling cascades, such as JAK/STAT3, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/β-catenin, Hippo/YAP, Notch, Hedgehog, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. In addition, we discussed how METTL3 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) by regulating immune responses and metabolic pathways promoting immune evasion and therapy resistance. Therapeutic strategies targeting METTL3-including small-molecule inhibitors, CRISPR-Cas9 approaches, combination immunotherapy, and tumor-selective delivery systems-are discussed together with the challenges that continue to limit clinical translation. Collectively, these findings position METTL3 as a central epitranscriptomic regulator of HCC progression; however, further mechanistic and clinical validation remains necessary to establish its utility as a therapeutic target and prognostic biomarker.

title: The Role of METTL3-Mediated m6A Methylation in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression and Treatment.

abstract: Some, but not all, gapmer antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) delivered into cerebrospinal fluid exhibit fatal subacute toxicity in late-stage prion-infected mice but not in uninfected mice. Here, we performed a battery of in vivo studies demonstrating that the toxicity is compound- and disease- stage-dependent, and not predicted by behavioral or molecular measurements in uninfected animals. A panel of toxic ASOs all elicited a consistent transcriptomic response signature in prion-infected mice, which emerged over the course of 7 days post dose. This signature, driven chiefly by decreased expression of a specific set of astrocyte-expressed genes, was absent in uninfected mice receiving the same ASOs, was absent, less intense, and/or more transient in infected mice receiving tolerated ASOs, and was distinct from the transcriptomic effect of prion disease itself. Our data argue that the toxicity is an interaction between ASO and prion disease at high doses for specific compounds, and does not represent an exacerbation of ASO toxicity nor of prion disease.

title: Antisense Oligonucleotides that Are Toxic to Prion-Infected Mice Share an Emergent Mechanism.

abstract: In this study, we developed a library of mRNA lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) containing clinically used ionizable lipids. We surface-modified these nanoparticles with heparosan polysaccharides and systematically compared their performance with conventional poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)-modified formulations. Our heparosan (HEP)-coated LNPs increased mRNA expression in dendritic and macrophage cell lines by up to ∼10-fold. Mechanistic studies using live-cell imaging and intracellular nanoparticle trafficking analysis revealed that HEP-modified LNPs exhibited reduced colocalization with late endosomal (Rab7+) and lysosomal (LAMP1+) compartments. These findings are consistent with enhanced endosomal escape of HEP-modified formulations. Repeated subcutaneous administrations of HEP-modified firefly luciferase mRNA-LNPs demonstrated sustained expression and distinct response dynamics in mice. We further observed significantly enhanced humoral anti-spike protein immune responses in mice after subcutaneous administration of HEP-modified LNPs containing SARS-CoV-2 spike S-2P mRNA. Histopathological evaluation and spleen immune cell profiling showed no observable toxicity or adverse effects. Overall, these results demonstrate the effects of HEP surface modification on mRNA LNP expression, intracellular trafficking, and in vivo activity, and support HEP-based surface engineering as a PEG-free approach for nucleic acid delivery and potential future applications in nanomedicine.

description: In observational studies, small daily doses of lithium have been associated with a 77% reduced risk of developing Parkinson's disease (PD). In addition, lithium therapy has been effective in preventing neuronal death and behavioral symptoms in several PD animal models. Recently, our group has shown 24-weeks of low-dose lithium therapy in PD to improve both MRI and blood-based biomarkers implying that lithium may be slowing the progression of the disease. However, these findings stem from only three of four patients receiving MRIs. A larger study will be required to determine if these promising results can be replicated. The proposed study will enroll 20 additional PD patients who will be randomly assigned to receive either lithium 20mg/day or identically-appearing placebo capsules for 24 weeks. This will be a double-blind study meaning that neither the patients nor the study team will know to which therapy patients have been assigned. Positive results from this study will support further research on lithium that could eventually support lithium as a disease-modifying therapy for PD that could improve patients' long-term prognoses.
